name: Liberty
overview: Scripture presents liberty as both a divine proclamation and a spiritual reality, exemplified by the year of jubilee when freedom and restoration were declared to all inhabitants of the land (Leviticus 25:10). Isaiah 61 emphasizes liberty as a message from the Lord to captives, symbolizing deliverance and healing through the anointed one. The repeated refrain in Judges highlights the absence of righteous leadership, where liberty without godly guidance leads to each person doing what is right in their own eyes, underscoring the need for Christ-centered liberty rather than mere political or figurative freedom.
